races.name: Racing Tv Club Day Novices' Hurdle Race (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Porcupine Bank
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old carries top weight at 162lbs and steps up from 16f to 2m6f, a trip that could expose or expose stamina; his three-from-three record on good ground is strong but Sean Bowen is 4/35 over 14 days for Elliott, softening the trainer angle slightly, and the [STYLE_FIT] tag notes he races somewhat out of his sharpest role here at this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Fine Thing
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton are in sharp form at 2/5 over 14 days, and Fine Thing's win at 20f on good ground is directly relevant to this 2m6f test on similar going; the five-year-old drops 10lb in OR to Porcupine Bank, giving the Harry Skelton mount a class concession to chase down, and his track record of 2/2 on similar going makes him a genuine player in this match.

races.paceDynamic: With only two runners declared, Porcupine Bank is the de facto pace-setter and will lead or race prominently throughout this 2m6f trip on good-to-firm ground at Stratford, setting a measured, uncontested tempo with no rival to pressurise him. Fine Thing, also a prominent racer by nature, will slot in directly behind or alongside, meaning there is no genuine pace battle and the race will be run at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. The absence of any hold-up horses or midfielders means this is a straightforward match race between two prominent types, with the winner likely decided by jumping fluency, fitness and class in the closing stages rather than any tactical manoeuvre. This race shape strongly favours the horse who can dictate or shadow the pace comfortably and who possesses superior stamina reserves for the final climb — a front-running or close-tracking profile wins here, and there is no scenario where a closer profits from a slow early pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Controls Match
scenarios.trigger: If Porcupine Bank dictates an unchallenged, steady gallop and jumps cleanly throughout.
scenarios.body: Porcupine Bank, with Gordon Elliott's horses in solid form and Sean Bowen aboard, controls every yard and the even pace suits his stamina at this longer trip; his three hurdle runs this season at 16f show consistent form and he steps up in trip here which could play to his strengths.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Fine Thing Matches And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Fine Thing, handled by the sharp Dan and Harry Skelton combination, tracks efficiently and outstays Porcupine Bank up the straight.
scenarios.body: Fine Thing's two wins at 20f and 16f on good ground show he handles this surface and trip profile well; the Skelton yard's 2/5 recent strike rate signals live form, and Harry Skelton may time his challenge to arrive late when Porcupine Bank's energy fades.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jumping Error Decides Outcome
scenarios.trigger: If either horse makes a significant jumping error mid-race that disrupts rhythm or causes a fall, gifting the other a simple lead.
scenarios.body: A two-runner race over 2m6f with multiple hurdles means a single blunder could be decisive; whichever horse jumps cleanly throughout will inherit a straightforward winning opportunity with no other rival to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sustained Battle Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If both horses match strides from the outset and race head-to-head for the entire trip, turning the contest into a genuine stamina test.
scenarios.body: An end-to-end duel on good-to-firm ground over this distance will drain both horses, meaning the one with the stronger hurdles record and superior class rating — Porcupine Bank at OR 130 — holds a marginal edge in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch Fine Thing's jumping — a clean round from Harry Skelton's mount is the single biggest variable in deciding whether he can match Porcupine Bank stride-for-stride over 2m6f.

Monitor Porcupine Bank's gallop early — if Sean Bowen sets too fast a pace for two runners over this trip on good-to-firm ground, the horse may tie up in the final stages and hand Fine Thing a winning chance.

The going report consistently lists this race as Good To Firm rather than the advertised Good — both runners are tagged going=OK but neither has extensive experience on genuinely fast ground, and conditions could sharpen the pace beyond sustainable levels.

With only two runners, any in-running incident such as a loose horse, a stumble at a hurdle, or rider error becomes instantly decisive — there is no third horse to fill the gap or exert alternative pressure.

races.name: Happy 70th Birthday Helen Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Notnowlinda
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old hold-up performer for the powerful Skelton yard, whose recent form includes a solid fourth on good ground; best watch is whether Harry Skelton can position her close enough to the pace over 2m6f to make her late effort count, as her 105-day absence is a minor query.|
runners_data.comment: Notnowlinda shaped with promise when third two starts back, and a rating of 112 puts her firmly in contention off 161 lb, though she remains winless in recent starts and the 105-day absence is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Rebel Tribesman
runners_data.note: The dominant pace influence — Jamie Snowden's five-year-old has a perfect five-from-five place record on similar going including two wins, a T14 strike rate of 2/2, and will face zero front-running competition here; the key question is whether he can sustain his lead over this extended 2m6f trip without being reeled in.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and in fine nick, Rebel Tribesman has won twice in his last five starts with a second last time out, and he has run over today's trip before; carrying 161 lb is the one query, but his rating of 118 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Kom Tu Voudras
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse by inclination — with a win and two places from five runs on good ground — that Harry Cobden will find shunted further forward than ideal given the field's composition; the tongue-tie is noted, and his STYLE_FIT flag means his chance should be tempered if the pace plays into the front-runner's hands.|
runners_data.comment: Kom Tu Voudras arrives here with two wins in her last five starts, including a victory three starts back, and 27 days between runs suggests she returns fresh and ready; the main risk is a stiff 161 lb to shoulder.

runners_data.name: Torrent
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has shown moderate consistency at best, going winless in five similar-going starts with a string of mid-pack finishes; Nigel Hawke's yard has no T14 runners to form view on, and Torrent will need a significant step up to trouble the principals, though the trip and going are not obvious concerns.|
runners_data.comment: Torrent shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out, and he has run over today's trip, making him a genuine threat from a workable 27-day break; the main concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Kittys Glance
runners_data.note: Alan King's five-year-old boasts a fine form profile — 1W5P on good/good-to-firm — but is a genuine hold-up type whose natural rear position is compromised in this shape; Tom Bellamy is an able judge of pace and may manufacture a useful midfield pitch, but the STYLE_FIT discount applies if the race stays truly steadily run throughout.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of five on our figures, Kittys Glance faces a stiff task under 156 lb, though her recent form reads encouragingly — second last time out, and a winner four starts back — and she arrives fresh after 48 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Rebel Tribesman is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and will dictate from the front over 2m6f on good-to-firm ground at Stratford, setting a sustainable and uncontested gallop with no rival likely to challenge for the lead. The remaining four runners — Notnowlinda, Kom Tu Voudras, Torrent, and Kittys Glance — are all hold-up or prominent types, meaning Rebel Tribesman faces zero pressure and can control the tempo entirely to suit himself. This field holds more hold-up types than the race map can place at the rear; Kom Tu Voudras and Kittys Glance are genuine closers by nature but are shown in midfield because the rearward slots are overcrowded, and neither is likely to secure their natural position in this shape. With a lone pace-setter dictating an honest but manageable tempo on quick ground over a staying trip, this race shape strongly favours the prominent/front-running profile — a horse that can travel comfortably just off or on the pace and sustain the effort to the line, rather than a pure hold-up type relying on a late surge that may never materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rebel Tribesman Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Rebel Tribesman jumps well, dictates his own pace, and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Rebel Tribesman sets a controlled, uncontested gallop, jumps fluently, and uses his superior front-running class — backed by a T14 of 2/2 and five-from-five place record on similar going — to sustain the effort and hold on. Horses travelling in midfield or rear find themselves with too much to do over a trip that does not play to a late-finishing style on this quick surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If Rebel Tribesman sets a stronger tempo than expected, opening the race up for a well-rated closer to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: A slightly more pressured pace stretches the field and creates enough of a frantic gallop that a chasing runner has genuine ground to make up in the final half-mile. Notnowlinda, the most experienced horse here at age 9, has the best hold-up profile and is ridden by Harry Skelton, who has the course craft to time a late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Kom Tu Voudras or Kittys Glance, forced into a more prominent position than usual, travel well enough to pounce turning for home.
scenarios.body: Displaced from their natural rear position, one of these two could find themselves in an unintentionally ideal stalking role just behind Rebel Tribesman, close enough to strike if he fades. Kittys Glance carries the stronger recent form profile — 1W5P on similar going — and Tom Bellamy's judgment of pace could make this scenario possible.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Torrent Improves Markedly
scenarios.trigger: If Torrent steps forward significantly from recent modest efforts and the pace suits a horse who needs a strong gallop to stay competitive.
scenarios.body: Torrent has shown flashes of ability over this sort of trip on good ground but has failed to convert, and his headgear (p) signals connections seeking improvement. If Rebel Tribesman's uncontested pace suits a horse that travels best when switched off early, Torrent could emerge as a surprise package in the closing stages.

watchPoints.text: Rebel Tribesman's jumping is critical — any hesitation or mistake at a hurdle will cost him the momentum advantage that is his entire tactical weapon in this shape.

Monitor whether Kom Tu Voudras or Kittys Glance get shuffled further back than mapped at the start; if both end up behind Notnowlinda, the hold-up end of this field becomes dangerously congested and late closers will be fighting for room.

Notnowlinda's 105-day layoff for the Skelton yard is worth tracking in-running — if she travels freely early she is likely fit and dangerous, but a laboured effort from the three-furlong pole would signal the break has taken a toll.

Torrent's hood application is worth noting — if he settles better than in recent outings and tracks Rebel Tribesman at a length or two, he could emerge as a value factor in Scenario D at a longer price than his form strictly warrants.

races.name: Brian And Sheila Vaughan Memorial Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Crebilly
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill with Harry Cobden aboard — a strong pairing — who returns from 53 days off with two recent placings on good ground at 24f; the step to 2m3½f is well within range and a genuine gallop is exactly what this type needs.|
runners_data.comment: Bounced back with a win two starts back and has experience over today's trip; Crebilly is the top-rated runner in this field and his 161 lb burden is the main query after 53 days off.

runners_data.name: Magistrato
runners_data.note: 152-day absence is the primary concern, but four wins from five starts on good ground at 20f for Deborah Cole's yard gives a striking profile once fit; natural prominent racer who travels well and has the form reading to be competitive first time back if tuned up at home.|
runners_data.comment: Magistrato won three of his last five starts, but our figures rank him bottom of this field and a 152-day absence adds doubt; the burden of 159 lb is sizeable, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Bagheera Ginge
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who arrives on the back of a win 52 days ago at 22f on good ground, with three wins from five good-ground runs and Sam Twiston-Davies retaining the ride; the challenge is Sir Tivo's presence, which means he cannot simply stride clear unchallenged.|
runners_data.comment: Bagheera Ginge arrives on the back of a win, has run over today's trip and going, and his record shows three wins in his last five starts — a horse in fine fettle. The one concern is a 52-day absence since that victory.

runners_data.name: Captain Cool
runners_data.note: Six-year-old in excellent recent form with three wins and three placings in his last six, all at shorter trips (16-17f) on good ground; the step to 2m3½f from 16-17f tests whether his finishing speed translates to a sterner stamina test — trainer Jennie Candlish is 3/8 in the last 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Captain Cool brings strong recent form to this contest — a winner two starts back and third last time out, with experience of today's trip and going and a solid rating of 131 to underpin his claims; the main concern is whether 32 days off the track has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Parisencore
runners_data.note: Decade-old hold-up type for Nicky Richards who drops down from 24f trips; his recent form reads 41-525 which is patchy, but the two wins came on good ground at 20f and his best asset is a thorough staying profile that could see him home if rivals crack.|
runners_data.comment: Parisencore shaped with promise when second two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, while his 134 rating underlines his standing as a leading danger here; the concern is that fifth last time out and 39 days off the track since.

runners_data.name: Sir Tivo
runners_data.note: 12-year-old confirmed front-runner with a recent win at 17f and consistent good-ground record; at this age over a longer trip his ability to sustain the lead all the way against the younger Bagheera Ginge is the core question, and a tiring finish is a real risk.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures, Sir Tivo faces a stiff ask under 156 lb, yet he arrives in decent heart — a winner last time out, 32 days ago, and he has experience of today's going.

races.paceDynamic: Bagheera Ginge and Sir Tivo are both confirmed front-runners, meaning the opening exchanges at Stratford over 2m3½f on good-to-firm ground will be genuinely contested rather than dawdled along — both jockeys (Sam Twiston-Davies and Sean Bowen) are proactive riders who will want position, so a true-run gallop is near-certain from the outset. That honest pace shapes a race that will test stamina reserves through the final fences, applying pressure on any horse that has to race keenly or burns energy early to secure its position. The prominent-to-midfield horses — Captain Cool, Magistrato, and the hold-up pair Crebilly and Parisencore — are all handed a track-pace that suits measured, efficient jumping and a well-timed challenge off the back of a genuine gallop. This race shape decisively favours the prominent and hold-up profiles: horses who can settle just off the pace, conserve energy across the first circuit, and produce a sustained finishing effort when the leaders begin to tie up approaching the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Genuine Gallop, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Bagheera Ginge and Sir Tivo set an honest, unrelenting pace that drains each other and softens the field for those held up or tracking.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners trade blows throughout, creating a strong gallop on good-to-firm ground that leaves them vulnerable late; horses who have settled off the pace in the first 1m4f arrive with untapped reserves at the business end.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine but Sir Tivo or Bagheera Ginge settles fractionally better than expected, allowing a prominent tracker to land close enough to pounce.
scenarios.body: Captain Cool's consistent recent form and proven good-ground speed make him the ideal beneficiary of a hot pace carried by rivals, as does Magistrato's strong course-type record of four wins in similar conditions; both can race prominently without burning their engines.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters — most likely Bagheera Ginge given superior recent form and Sam Twiston-Davies's tactical reading — establishes a clear lead while Sir Tivo fades.
scenarios.body: Bagheera Ginge's three wins at this going range and the trainer's eye for placing horses makes an unchallenged-enough lead plausible if Sir Tivo underperforms early; a controlled gallop lets the leader dictate and the race never truly tests its stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail, Race Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves too hot too early and the race deteriorates into a slog, rewarding the horse with the highest raw stamina rather than finishing pace.
scenarios.body: At 10 years of age Parisencore has the profile of a stayer who can grind through a truly severe test, and Crebilly's hold-up style means it arrives fresh; however this scenario requires an extreme burn-up that remains unlikely given the moderate field size.

watchPoints.text: Bagheera Ginge and Sir Tivo will fight for the same piece of real estate from the off — watch the opening half-mile closely, as an overly aggressive early duel between the two could burn both out long before the final fence.

Magistrato's 152-day absence is a significant fitness flag; if he moves with his usual fluency early and travels sweetly, he becomes a live danger, but any sign of ring-rustiness in his jumping should temper confidence sharply.

Captain Cool has not been asked to travel beyond 17f in his recent starts — monitor whether he jumps fluently and travels comfortably in the 2m3½f context, particularly from the halfway point, as this is his first serious stamina test.

Good-to-firm ground is confirmed for this race — all six runners carry an OK going tag, but Bagheera Ginge's dominant sim-going strike rate (14/15) stands out and is worth noting when interpreting any market moves in the final hour.

Crebilly has had 53 days off and Magistrato 152 days — should either show race-morning market support, their fitness levels have clearly satisfied connections, which would materially upgrade their chance in what is otherwise a wide-open staying contest.

races.name: Quinnbet Novices' Limited Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Dunkerque
runners_data.note: Boasts four wins from his last five, all on Good ground, and carries the joint-highest OR at 128 — Sean Quinlan will ride him prominently just behind Krak, hunting the leader throughout; the form figures scream a horse in the form of his life, and the Jennie Candlish yard is firing with a 3/8 14-day strike rate.
runners_data.comment: Dunkerque won four of his last five starts, with a runner-up finish last time out the only blemish, and he returns after 31 days in excellent recent nick; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 164 lb is the one query against a confident profile.

runners_data.name: Samuel Spade
runners_data.note: Races from hold-up, which is a structural problem in a three-runner race where only one horse is setting the pace — Beau Morgan (claiming 5lb) will need something to go wrong ahead of him to manufacture a winning run, as his sim-going record of 2W from 15 runs is notably modest; best form comes over 23-24f which gives him a slight distance edge.
runners_data.comment: Samuel Spade caught the eye with a win three starts back and returns here in solid nick after 36 days off, his experience over today's trip and a rating of 127 marking him as a leading threat; the worry is he was only fifth two starts back.

runners_data.name: Krak
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: Harry Skelton will send him straight to the front and control the tempo entirely, and the Skelton yard's 2/5 recent record underlines stable confidence; he carries the lowest weight at 152lbs, has placed on similar going in his last three runs, but his 0W from 3P on sim-going is the key flag — he sets the pace but has not yet won from the front.
runners_data.comment: Krak has shaped with plenty of promise in recent starts, finishing third last time out and second three starts back, and he arrives here fresh enough after 31 days off carrying 152 lb; the main risk is that he remains yet to win in his last five starts.

races.paceDynamic: Krak is the sole confirmed front-runner and will set off to lead from the outset over this 2m6½f trip on Good to Firm ground at Stratford, with no rival likely to dispute that position — Dunkerque is a prominent-racing type who will sit just off the pace, and Samuel Spade is a hold-up horse who will be content to track from the rear. With Harry Skelton in the saddle for the in-form Dan Skelton yard, Krak will be allowed to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than being forced into a lung-busting duel, which fundamentally shapes this as a mucker's-heaven front-running affair. The key question is whether Krak can maintain that lead into the home straight or whether Dunkerque, hunting him from close range throughout, can reel him in late. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the prominent-to-lead profile: a lone leader controlling tempo on Good to Firm ground over a staying trip gives the front-running and prominent types a material tactical edge, while the lone hold-up runner Samuel Spade faces the dual burden of conceding ground and having limited targets to aim at in a three-runner field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Krak Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Krak bowls along at a measured pace and Dunkerque cannot close the gap approaching the final fences.
scenarios.body: Krak enjoys total control of the tempo with Harry Skelton able to manage the race from the front, conserving enough for a finishing effort over the last two fences; on Good to Firm ground this trip rewards a horse that jumps cleanly and travels smoothly, which suits Krak's profile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Dunkerque Reels Krak In
scenarios.trigger: If Dunkerque travels powerfully throughout and gradually wears down Krak between the last two fences.
scenarios.body: Dunkerque's excellent recent form — four wins from his last five starts on Good ground — marks him as the improver in the race, and Sean Quinlan will be watching Krak's every move from close range; if Krak's stride shortens late, Dunkerque's persistent jumping ability and class advantage off OR 128 sees him collar the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Samuel Spade Late Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong early, burning out Krak, and Samuel Spade produces a powerful staying finish from the rear.
scenarios.body: Samuel Spade's hold-up style is structurally disadvantaged in a three-runner race with only one confirmed front-runner setting a likely steady tempo, but if conditions play faster than expected and the pace proves genuinely searching, Beau Morgan could produce him with a late run; his two wins on similar ground and his form at this trip give him an outside chance in that specific scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Errors Shuffle Order
scenarios.trigger: If one or more horses make a significant jumping error that disrupts the natural running order mid-race.
scenarios.body: With fences to jump over 2m6½f there is always the possibility that a mistake from Krak or Dunkerque reshuffles the field entirely; in that case the horse least inconvenienced by the incident — whether it benefits Dunkerque by inheriting the lead or Samuel Spade by closing ground — profits, but this outcome depends entirely on an incident rather than tactics.

watchPoints.text: Krak's 0W-from-3P record on similar going is the headline concern — watch whether Harry Skelton gets a clean round of jumping, as any fence error for the sole front-runner could trigger a dramatic reshuffle.

Dunkerque's proximity to Krak throughout the race is critical — if Sean Quinlan is able to sit within a length or two turning for home, the strongly in-form Dunkerque becomes a serious danger to the leader at the final fences.

Samuel Spade's 5lb claimer Beau Morgan adds uncertainty in a small field — watch how aggressively he rides for position early, as a three-runner race with a steady pace may force him to adapt away from his natural hold-up style.

Going reported as Good to Firm at Stratford all card — faster than the declared Good, which plays into the hands of horses with proven form on quick ground; Dunkerque's sim-going record of 12/15 5W6P is significantly stronger than Samuel Spade's 8/15 2W5P in this context.

races.name: Happy Birthday Sue Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Glenmalure Flyer
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton's booking for Dan Skelton is the standout jockey-trainer combination in the race; a genuine hold-up horse with two wins at Good ground over distance, returning from 51 days off in form that includes a recent win, ideally suited by the expected hot pace over 3m3½f.
runners_data.comment: Glenmalure Flyer arrives here as a dual winner in her last five starts, with a third last time out no great setback in a lively recent spell, and she handles today's going, making her the one to beat off 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Winning Paddy
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up horse with a win over 26f on Good ground and solid course form at Stratford-like tracks; Richie McLernon takes over for Alexandra Dunn whose T14 record reads a rare but sharp 1/1, and 48 days off is a manageable gap for a horse whose profile suits this race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Winning Paddy showed he knows how to get his head in front with a win three starts back, and at 160 lb he carries a stiff weight burden that may just blunt his finishing effort after 48 days off.

runners_data.name: Yes And Yes
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back wins over marathon Good-ground trips confirm genuine staying ability, but this horse's natural style is hold-up — the field's depth of rearward types means it is likely to end up racing closer to the pace than it would prefer, with the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflecting that compromise in race position.
runners_data.comment: Yes And Yes arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip, making him a serious threat, though 92 days off the track is the obvious query on fitness.

runners_data.name: Illogical Logic
runners_data.note: The highest-rated of the confirmed front-runners at OR 81, Jack Tudor is a capable operator for Christian Williams, but a recent form string of 346P-5 offers limited encouragement and the horse will need to manage a three-way pace battle over a demanding 3m3½f without burning out.

runners_data.name: Flashy Boy
runners_data.note: An honest front-runner for Robbie Llewellyn, freshest in the field at 32 days since last run, but his Good-ground record shows zero wins or places in nine runs on that surface and his form string of P1P-45 is patchy — likely to help set a fierce pace rather than profit from it.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up twice in his last five starts makes Flashy Boy hard to fancy, and he ranks last on our figures here; a winner four starts back offers some encouragement, but two non-completions in recent form are a significant concern.

runners_data.name: The Kings Soldier
runners_data.note: A young five-year-old tackling a very long 3m3½f trip, ridden by a 7lb-claiming amateur in Oscar Palmer, and form figures of 4-6335 suggest consistency without winning potency; going is fine, but age, trip, and inexperienced pilot all point to a horse that contributes to the pace rather than dictating the outcome.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked fifth of six on our figures, The Kings Soldier faces a stiff ask here, though back-to-back thirds two and three starts ago hint at some consistency, and 55 days between runs leaves him fresh if not perhaps race-fit.

races.paceDynamic: Illogical Logic, Flashy Boy, and The Kings Soldier are all confirmed front-runners, meaning this 3m3½f chase over Good to Firm ground at Stratford will be run at a genuine, unrelenting gallop from the outset — there is no scenario where these three cede the early pace voluntarily. The prolonged battle for supremacy up front will burn through the field's stamina reserves across the marathon trip, creating a race that almost inevitably sets up for those able to sit off the pace and pick up the pieces. Yes And Yes is a genuine hold-up type who has been mapped to midfield because the field holds more hold-up runners than the rear of the map can accommodate — Glenmalure Flyer and Winning Paddy are the true back-markers most likely to secure genuine rearward positions, while Yes And Yes is the one most likely to end up slightly closer than natural. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the patient hold-up profile — horses that can switch off behind a hot pace, conserve energy, and motor through beaten rivals from the home turn — making Glenmalure Flyer and Winning Paddy the most structurally advantaged runners given how the race will be framed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out over the extended 3m3½f trip, leaving the hold-up horses to cruise through on the bridle.
scenarios.body: The ferocious early gallop set by Illogical Logic, Flashy Boy, and The Kings Soldier drains the field up front, and the marathon distance ensures attrition bites hard in the final mile; patient hold-up horses travelling well in rear are perfectly positioned to capitalise. Glenmalure Flyer and Winning Paddy, both proven over big distances on Good ground with strong hold-up profiles and capable jockeys, are structurally best placed to collect.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacemaker Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners finds a better rhythm than the others and is allowed to coast at a sustainable lead while rivals fight behind.
scenarios.body: Illogical Logic is the highest-rated of the front-runners and has shown enough form at distance on Good ground to be the one most likely to establish a workable lead if infighting among front-runners creates separation early; Jack Tudor's experience in managing front-running horses adds tactical credibility. In this shape, a well-conserved prominent horse who tracks the leader without burning petrol could also land a blow late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is hot but not chaotic and a horse travelling prominently off the leaders attacks the last two fences with energy to spare.
scenarios.body: Yes And Yes, though mapped to midfield due to redistribution, is a genuine hold-up type whose two recent wins over marathon Good ground mark it as a serious stayer; if it secures a closer position than expected and the pacemakers fold, it could be the one emerging late. The STYLE_FIT concern tempers confidence here — racing out of its natural role reduces the probability this shape delivers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is miscalculated and one front-runner gets an uncontested lead at a manageable gallop, conserving enough to hold on.
scenarios.body: With three horses wanting the front, an outright uncontested lead is unlikely, but if early jostling settles quickly and one horse — most plausibly Illogical Logic given OR advantage among the front-runners — steals a march unchallenged, stamina reserves could prove sufficient over the trip. This is the least likely shape given the confirmed three-way pace battle, but the possibility cannot be entirely dismissed in a six-runner field.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Illogical Logic, Flashy Boy, and The Kings Soldier race aggressively into the first few fences — if all three fight for the lead immediately, the pace could become dangerously fast and set the race up exclusively for Glenmalure Flyer and Winning Paddy.

Flashy Boy has zero wins or places in nine runs on Good or Good to Firm ground — if going reports continue to drift towards the quicker end, his ability to contribute meaningfully to the pace without folding on the final circuit is questionable.

Yes And Yes has been mapped to midfield due to redistribution but is a natural hold-up type — watch at the start whether Lee Edwards can slot in closer to the rear as intended or is forced forward by the field dynamic, which would compromise its race shape entirely.

The Kings Soldier's five-year-old jumping profile over the longest trip in the race with an amateur claimer deserves monitoring at the early fences — any jumping error or loss of rhythm could create interference for horses travelling behind in the hold-up group.

Glenmalure Flyer's last three runs at 16f suggest Dan Skelton has been dropping him in trip — stepping sharply back up to 27f today returns him to the distance where his best form sits, and Harry Skelton's record of managing hold-up horses in staying chases is worth tracking as the field fans out from the home turn.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Reteti
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with solid sim-going record of 10/15 on good, placing four times in that sample; Marc Goldstein partners for Sheena West and the horse carries a hood, suggesting settling is key — needs a rough-and-tumble finish to find daylight from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Reteti arrives here winless in his last five starts but has been consistently competitive, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, and his profile — experience over today's trip and going, a solid official mark of 100, and a rating of 106 that tops this field — makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Eyeeye
runners_data.note: Brendan Powell picks up the ride on a horse that fades in the finish — a flagged tendency that is a material concern in a steadily-run race where any weakness late will be ruthlessly exposed; 0W3P sim-going record reflects consistent placed effort but no winning punch.
runners_data.comment: Eyeeye arrives here 22 days fresh and has run over today's trip, but he is winless in his last five starts, with only a second three starts back to encourage connections; carrying 168 lb against a field where our rating of 100 ranks him fifth of twelve suggests a midfield finish looks the likeliest outcome.

runners_data.name: Versatile
runners_data.note: Jonathan Burke partners the five-year-old who carries a hood and shows a consistent pattern of running in fourth-to-third positions; 8/15 sim-going record is modest, but the placed form on good ground keeps him relevant if the race produces traffic trouble.
runners_data.comment: Rated 102 and ranked second of the twelve runners, Versatile arrives on the back of a third three starts back and is no stranger to today's trip and conditions, making him a live threat; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts, capped by a disappointing ninth last time out.

runners_data.name: Jet Patrol
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen, a major jockey booking, rides a hold-up horse who has won twice on good going and finished in the frame ten times in fifteen similar-ground starts — the standout sim-going record among the hold-up brigade and a serious each-way proposition if he can find a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Jet Patrol landed a win five starts back but has posted a fifth, fourth and sixth in more recent outings, suggesting his form is patchy at best; he has experience over today's trip and going, and 27 days between runs leaves him fairly fresh.

runners_data.name: Diesel Line
runners_data.note: James Bowen partners a true hold-up performer with two wins at this trip on good ground, but the horse is mapped to midfield because the rear of the field is overcrowded; racing out of its natural position tempers its chance materially, and a style-fit score of 0.93 reflects that discount.
runners_data.comment: Diesel Line has experience of today's trip and conditions, and our rating of 101 puts him ahead of his official mark — the case for an improved effort is real, though he is yet to win in his last five starts and a seventh last time out is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Mayday Games
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field; Kielan Woods can dictate terms unchallenged, and a recent win on good ground confirms going suitability — the race shape is built around him, and his ability to control fractions makes him dangerous if he has the class to hold on.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back but has also fallen and posted an unplaced effort in recent starts, giving a mixed picture; he has run over today's trip and returns after 27 days off carrying 160 lb, with our rating of 93 suggesting he sits just in mid-division.

runners_data.name: Lord Cauvelliere
runners_data.note: Sean Houlihan rides a five-year-old who has been consistently placed across seven good-ground runs (1W2P) and is suited by a prominent, tracking style; 78 days off the track is a stamina of freshness question, but the sim-going record is perfect and the position behind the leader suits this scenario best.
runners_data.comment: Lord Cauvelliere has shown enough consistency in recent starts to make him a genuine threat here, and our rating of 102 suggests he is better than his official mark of 91 indicates — the main risk is that he arrives 78 days fresh and is yet to score in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Clever Relation
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor takes the mount on a horse whose natural home is at the back of the field — placed into midfield here simply because the hold-up zone is oversubscribed; the recent second on good ground is the key piece of form, but a style-fit score of 0.92 means it needs a significant piece of luck to reproduce that effort from its mapped position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, including a pull-up, and ranked last on our figures, Clever Relation faces a stiff task off 153 lb after 77 days away, though he has run over today's trip before and that recent second offers a crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Berry Edge
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton — a top-level jockey booking — partners a horse returning from 156 days off the track with all five recent starts on soft ground and zero wins or places on good-to-firm; the going looks a genuine concern, and although Skelton's ability is undoubted, the horse's true hold-up style is further compromised by being pushed into midfield in a congested field.
runners_data.comment: Berry Edge is a long way down the rankings on our figures, and a 156-day absence is a significant query; he does at least return on the back of a win two starts back and has run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Glance At Me
runners_data.note: Shane Quinlan (3lb claimer) aboard a horse returning from 793 days off — a massive absence that demands caution; the 2W4P sim-going record on good ground is intriguing and headgear pointers (hg: ht) suggest connections have tried to sharpen him, but the layoff makes any confidence extremely difficult.
runners_data.comment: Two consecutive pulls-up are a major concern, and 793 days off the track demands a significant leap of faith; but she has run over today's trip and her sole win in recent starts came four starts back, suggesting ability when right.

runners_data.name: Northern Rose
runners_data.note: James Davies partners the most consistent horse in the field — 1W8P on good going across fifteen similar-ground starts, including a recent second and a win; a prominent style that can press the front-runner makes her ideally positioned in this race shape, and she is the one horse whose natural role fits the unfolding scenario perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below the field on our figures, Northern Rose carries a hefty 151 lb and faces a stiff ask, though her recent form reads well with a win last time out and placed efforts filling much of the rest of her last five starts; she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Angel Of My Dreams
runners_data.note: Nick Slatter (3lb claimer) takes over on a five-year-old whose true running style is hold-up — pushed into midfield here because the rear is congested; a style-fit score of 0.91 signals a meaningful discount, and while the recent third on good ground shows some ability, the combination of claim, redistribution, and OR of 66 limits expectations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Angel Of My Dreams faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and returns from a 32-day break showing a shade more form than her official mark of 66 suggests, with a third and second in recent starts offering faint encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Mayday Games is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to contest the lead from the jump, Kielan Woods can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over 2m½f at Stratford. Lord Cauvelliere and Northern Rose are the likeliest horses to press from prominent positions, but neither is a committed front-runner, so the pace should be steady rather than pressurised. This field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Diesel Line, Clever Relation, Berry Edge, and Angel Of My Dreams are all natural hold-up horses pushed into midfield slots, meaning the true back of the field is less congested than it appears and several of these horses will struggle to find their ideal wide, late run. With a single pace-setter controlling fractions on fast summer ground and a cluster of prominent-to-midfield types just behind, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in behind the leader, quicken when the tempo lifts two out, and handle a genuinely decent surface — the prominent-to-midfield profile with tactical cruising speed holds the clearest edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mayday Games Controls, Followers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Mayday Games sets a measured gallop and the race is won by a horse tracking within two lengths of the lead from the second flight.
scenarios.body: Mayday Games dictates at a fair but uncontested clip on the good-to-firm ground, and when he quickens jumping two out the horse closest to him in the prominent group inherits the advantage before hold-up types can mount a challenge from off the pace; Northern Rose's consistent second-and-first form and perfect sim-going record make her ideally placed, while Lord Cauvelliere's prominent style suits the pattern.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace results in a falsely-run race and one of the redistributed true hold-up types finds enough daylight to close powerfully from the rear.
scenarios.body: Mayday Games's uncontested lead could turn into a crawl that compresses the field, and if the tempo only picks up sharply from the third-last a genuine closer that manages to work wide and build momentum could hit the line fastest; Clever Relation's recent second on good ground and Jet Patrol's two wins from similar conditions give them credibility if they find a clear passage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Northern Rose Dictates From Front
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Rose's rider pushes forward to contest the lead with Mayday Games, injecting more pace and stretching the field into a true-run race.
scenarios.body: Should James Davies elect to commit early and test Mayday Games, the resulting stronger gallop suits hold-up horses more than usual but also risks pulling Northern Rose's stamina into play; if she handles the injection of pace and gets first run jumping the last, her proven course form on good and her 1W8P sim-going record make her a genuine threat to hold on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Crowding, Each-Way Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If traffic trouble in the pack — inevitable with several hold-up types fighting for the same ground — produces interference that scrambles the finishing order.
scenarios.body: With four redistributed hold-up horses all seeking wide runs from positions they did not naturally select, collisions and checking movements two out are a real risk, and a horse who manages to sidestep the trouble while sitting handy will benefit disproportionately; Versatile's consistent placed form and Glance At Me's each-way credentials at big odds could capitalise on the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Mayday Games must be monitored from the start — if he is allowed to slip the field unchallenged at the top of the back straight, the prominent horses behind him may have already conceded an unassailable advantage before they realise the pace has been set.

Northern Rose jumping into a contested lead with Mayday Games would fundamentally alter the race shape; watch James Davies's early tactics — any move to press rather than track will trigger Scenario C and shift the advantage toward the hold-up horses.

The cluster of four redistributed hold-up types (Diesel Line, Clever Relation, Berry Edge, Angel Of My Dreams) all seeking wide runs from midfield creates a high-risk traffic situation two out — a horse checking or being carried wide could take others with it.

Berry Edge's going is a live concern on good-to-firm after five consecutive soft-ground runs; Harry Skelton will know quickly whether the surface is cutting into the horse's action, and a laboured jumping display should be taken as a significant negative signal.

Glance At Me's 793-day absence makes him almost impossible to assess on form — watch his paddock demeanour and early race behaviour as the primary indicators of whether connections genuinely believe he is ready to fire fresh.
